sets.title: Same Subject Rule
sets.description: Identify correct and incorrect verbal adverb usage
sets.descriptionRussian: Определите правильное и неправильное употребление деепричастий

items.promptEnglish: Which sentence correctly uses the verbal adverb?
items.hint: Same subject: она услышала, она обрадовалась.
items.explanation: Same subject (она) in both parts. The other options have different subjects.

items.prompt: Why is 'Выходя из дома, пошёл дождь' wrong?
items.hint: Who was leaving? Who started raining?
items.explanation: The person leaving and the rain starting are different subjects. Verbal adverbs require the same subject.

items.prompt: Fix: 'Гуляя в парке, начался дождь.' The correct version is:
items.promptEnglish: Different subjects need a когда clause.
options: Когда я гулял в парке, начался дождь.
items.answer: Когда я гулял в парке, начался дождь.
items.hint: Different subjects: use когда clause instead.
items.explanation: Different subjects (I walked, rain started) require a когда clause, not a verbal adverb.

items.promptEnglish: Which sentence correctly uses the verbal adverb?
items.hint: Same subject: я закончил, я пошёл.
items.explanation: Same subject (я) in both clauses. The other options have different or missing subjects.

items.promptEnglish: Which uses a verbal adverb incorrectly?
options: Войдя в комнату, он снял пальто.
Не зная адреса, она спросила прохожего.
Проснувшись рано, на улице было тихо.
Думая о проблеме, он нашёл решение.
items.answer: Проснувшись рано, на улице было тихо.
items.hint: 'На улице было тихо' is impersonal (no subject to match).
items.explanation: Impersonal clause 'было тихо' has no subject. The person who woke up can't match it.

items.prompt: Verbal adverbs CANNOT be used when:
options: The main clause has a future verb
The subjects of the two actions are different
items.answer: The subjects of the two actions are different
items.explanation: Verbal adverbs require the same subject for both actions. Different subjects = use когда/пока.

sets.title: Position and Style
sets.description: Practice verbal adverb placement and register

items.prompt: Не _____ русского языка, турист попросил помощи. (Not knowing Russian, the tourist asked for help.)
items.promptEnglish: Not knowing Russian, the tourist asked for help.
items.hint: Not knowing (negated impf verbal adverb): не зная.
items.explanation: Negation + impf verbal adverb: не зная (not knowing). Same subject: турист.

items.promptEnglish: The verbal adverb and the main verb must share one subject.
items.hint: Who reads must also do the second action.
items.explanation: Same-subject rule: only я both reads (читая) and hears (услышал). The others have a different subject (telephone, rain).

items.prompt: In everyday speech, «Придя домой, она отдохнула» is most naturally said as:
items.promptEnglish: Verbal adverbs are bookish; spoken Russian prefers a clause.
options: Когда она пришла домой, она отдохнула.
items.answer: Когда она пришла домой, она отдохнула.
items.hint: Spoken style replaces the verbal adverb with a когда clause.
items.explanation: Verbal adverbs sound formal/written. In speech a когда clause is more natural: Когда она пришла домой...

minimalPairs.context: _____ по улице, я встретил друга. (same subject, correct)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: While walking, I met a friend. (correct usage)
minimalPairs.explanation: Same subject (я): verbal adverb is correct and more formal.

minimalPairs.context: _____ по улице, начался дождь. (different subjects, needs fix)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: While I walked, rain started. (different subjects)
minimalPairs.explanation: Different subjects (I, rain): must use когда clause.

sets.title: Negation and Reflexive Forms
sets.description: Practice negated and reflexive verbal adverbs

blanks: _____ дороги, мы заблудились. (Not knowing the road, we got lost.)
_____ утром, он опоздал на работу. (Having overslept in the morning, he was late for work.)
_____ домой, она увидела соседа. (While returning home, she saw her neighbor.)
_____ ничего, он ушёл. (Not having said anything, he left.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Negation (не + verbal adverb) and reflexive forms (-сь)
hints: Not knowing (negated impf): не + зная. Same subject: мы.
Having overslept (pf prior action): from проспать → проспав.
While returning (impf reflexive simultaneous): from возвращаться → возвращаясь.
Not having said (negated pf prior action): не + сказав.
explanations: Не зная: negation + impf verbal adverb. Не + зная (separate words). Same subject: мы.
Проспав: pf verbal adverb of проспать. Prior action: first overslept, then was late.
Возвращаясь: impf reflexive verbal adverb. Reflexive -сь added after -я. Simultaneous.
Не сказав: negation + pf verbal adverb. Не + сказав (separate words). Prior action.

items.prompt: In spoken Russian, verbal adverbs are often replaced by:
items.hint: Verbal adverbs are formal/written. Spoken Russian prefers...
items.explanation: Verbal adverbs are bookish. Spoken Russian prefers когда/пока clauses.

options: Когда я читал книгу, я пил чай.
Я читал книгу и пил чай.
Я пил чай, когда читал книгу.
items.explanation: The verbal adverb construction (Читая книгу...) is more formal/literary than когда or и.

items.prompt: Can this use a verbal adverb? 'Когда мы приехали, все уже ушли.'
items.promptEnglish: Both subjects are 'мы' and 'все' (different). Can you use a verbal adverb?
options: No, subjects are different (мы vs все)
items.answer: No, subjects are different (мы vs все)
items.hint: We arrived, but everyone had left. Two different groups.
items.explanation: Мы (we) and все (everyone) are different subjects. Cannot use a verbal adverb.

sets.title: Mixed Challenge
sets.description: Comprehensive usage drill combining all rules

items.prompt: _____ в комнату, он поздоровался. (Having entered the room, he said hello.)
items.promptEnglish: Having entered the room, he said hello.
items.hint: First entered, then greeted. Prior completed = perfective.
items.explanation: Prior completed action: войдя (pf verbal adverb of войти). Same subject: он.

items.prompt: _____ экзамены, студенты отдыхали. (Having passed the exams, the students relaxed.)
items.promptEnglish: Having passed the exams, the students relaxed.
items.hint: First passed exams, then relaxed. Prior = perfective. Same subject: студенты.
items.explanation: Prior completed, same subject: сдав (pf verbal adverb of сдать).

items.promptEnglish: Which correctly uses a verbal adverb?
options: Подъезжая к станции, поезд замедлил ход.
Приехав на вокзал, было уже поздно.
items.answer: Подъезжая к станции, поезд замедлил ход.
items.hint: The train is approaching AND slowing down. Same subject: поезд.
items.explanation: Same subject (поезд): the train approaches and slows. All others have different subjects.

items.prompt: Не _____ ответа, она продолжала ждать. (Not having received an answer, she continued to wait.)
items.promptEnglish: Not having received an answer, she continued to wait.
items.hint: Not received (negated pf prior action): не получив.
items.explanation: Negated perfective verbal adverb: не получив (not having received). Same subject: она.

translation.english: While working, he listened to music.
Having arrived at the station, we bought tickets.
translation.answer: Приехав на вокзал, мы купили билеты.
acceptableVariants: Прибыв на вокзал, мы купили билеты.

translation.english: Not understanding the question, he asked again.
